observation.visible_scene: Close-up view through a sharply focused silver metal wire grid (basket/cart wall) with a bent top rail. Behind the grid, out of focus, is an orange bottle-shaped object with a rounded base, set against a blurred background containing a dark blue-black region and a tan/beige region on the right. A small green blurred shape sits at the bottom-left.
visible_changes: The orange object translates from a center-left, upright orientation at t=0 toward the upper-right of the frame over roughly the first 0.7 seconds.
As it moves, the object tilts/rotates so that its rounded base (with its curved internal contour) turns to face the camera more directly, becoming the dominant visible part.
From about t=0.76 to the end (t=1.60), the orange object holds an approximately fixed position in the upper-right, with only minor jitter.

The foreground metal grid remains stationary and in focus throughout; its wire positions do not shift between frames, indicating the camera is fixed relative to the grid while the orange object moves within the frame.
The blurred background regions stay largely in place, with slight apparent changes consistent with the moving orange object altering occlusion rather than a camera pan.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the orange object is (bottle, container, etc.) and what material it is made of.
Whether the object is being held, placed, or removed by an unseen person, and any action before t=0 or after t=1.60.
The true 3D depth and orientation of the object behind the grid.
uncertain_details: The cause of the object's motion (hand movement vs. other) is not visible.
Whether any subtle background shift is due to camera micro-motion or to the object moving in depth; the grid itself is clearly static.
Exact rotation axis of the orange object is inferred only from the changing visibility of its rounded base.
